text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:
- Some 35,000 people gathered in Berne on Saturday to stage a peaceful protest against the government's planned public-sector job and wage cuts.
- Poland now thinks the agreement it made with Switzerland in 1949, under which the Swiss bank account funds of Polish citizens who died in World War Two would be turned over to Poland, was illegal.

- Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti rejects U.S. Senator D'Amato's accusations that Switzerland is hindering investigations into Holocaust victims' Swiss bank accounts, saying they were insulting and absolutely unacceptable. Thomas Borer - Cotti's troubleshooter and task force leader - is attempting to change the negative attitude towards Switzerland held by foreigners, particularly Americans.
- Usines metallurgiques de Vallorbe (UMV) posted a 3.3 percent decline in sales to 44.6 million Swiss francs for the 1995/96 fiscal year. Profit sank by 10.3 percent to 0.9 million francs.

- Swiss Federal Court is making Geneva treat jobless persons from other cantons the same as those with resident status. Up to now people living in the canton of Geneva for a minimum of one year were eligible to receive unemployment benefits.
